items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Chano Channel in the context of Dizzy Gillespie's opinions and band arrangements, but the interviewee (Mario Bauza) does not explicitly state a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction with Chano Channel in the provided text.

ctx.x: He got -- he's kicking, toying and toying and (inaudible). The only disillusion he have, after Chano got killed, he try -- he try everybody, and he say, I don't want anybody. I don't want no trumpet players in my band, because seems to me like they all play the same way, and there's no way near the way Channel played.

Chano Channel was the type of guy that (inaudible) arrangements (inaudible). He hear the band play. (Inaudible) like Chick Webb used to do. They had a way to play, a rhythm for that particular arrangement. (Inaudible). And this was a congo player (inaudible). And that's the way they play practically for everything. But Chano had a (inaudible) rhythm. That's

what Dizzy would say.
So keeping Dizzy out of sight all the time.
